who: B. Richard (Barry Richard) Burg, historian at Arizona State University, PhD University of Colorado.

evidence.says: ASU lists B. Richard Burg as professor of history, appointed in 1967, with a PhD from the University of Colorado.
The authority identifies B. R. as Barry Richard, includes B. Richard Burg as a variant, and records his Arizona State history affiliation.

notes: Name variants, university and doctoral institution agree.

who: Ian Campbell, historian of the Russian Empire at UC Davis since 2012, PhD history Michigan 2011.

evidence.says: UC Davis gives a Michigan history PhD in 2011 and appointment at Davis in 2012; research concerns the Russian Empire.
Bandeali’s title page names Ian Campbell as committee chair at UC Davis; it identifies the work as an MA thesis, dated 2023.
The ORCID candidate lists Reader in Early Modern Irish History at Queen’s University Belfast.
The other candidate is Ian Leslie Campbell, author of The Addis Ababa Massacre and a specialist in Ethiopia’s Italian occupation.

notes: Neither candidate is the Davis historian. The supplied student record also differs from the repository in degree and year.

who: Wendell Robert Carr Jr., historian of British and American intellectual history, Wisconsin 1972–1975, PhD Harvard 1967.

evidence.says: The Patriot Ledger obituary records W. Robert Carr’s Harvard history PhD in 1967 and teaching at Wisconsin from 1972 to 1975.
The candidate authority identifies William Carr, professor of history at Sheffield, with a Birmingham PhD in 1955.

notes: The Wisconsin supervisor and the Sheffield historian are different people.

who: John Carson, historian of science and the human sciences at Michigan, PhD Princeton 1994.

evidence.says: Michigan lists John Carson in History, PhD Princeton 1994, and identifies his book The Measure of Merit.
Merchant’s 2015 Michigan history dissertation names Associate Professor John Carson as doctoral committee chair.
The candidate authority is John Carson, author of The Measure of Merit, and links to Wikidata Q42907795.

notes: Direct supervision evidence, doctorate and the candidate’s identified work agree.

who: Kevin P. Coleman, historian of modern Latin America at Toronto Mississauga, PhD Indiana University Bloomington.

evidence.says: Toronto identifies Kevin P. Coleman as associate professor of history, with an Indiana PhD and research on modern Latin America and photography.
Kathleen Coleman is Harvard’s James Loeb Professor of Classics; her fields include Latin literature and Roman social history.
The candidate item identifies Kathleen M. Coleman, also named K. M. Coleman, and records her Harvard affiliation.

notes: Kevin P. Coleman and Kathleen M. Coleman are different scholars.

who: Christopher Michael Curtis, historian of early America and legal history, Iowa State 2003–2007, PhD Emory 2002.

evidence.says: Georgia Southern records an Emory history PhD in 2002, Iowa State appointment in 2003–2007, and subsequent history department leadership at Claflin.
The university’s dissertation record gives the full name Christopher Michael Curtis and an Emory history doctorate in 2002.
The candidate authority identifies Christopher Michael Curtis, author of Jefferson’s Freeholders, as a Claflin history professor and department chair.

notes: Full name, doctorate and institutional sequence agree. His Iowa State employment ended before the student’s 2009 completion.

who: Apparently Jack L. Davis, Greek archaeologist at Illinois Chicago 1977–1993, PhD Cincinnati 1977.

evidence.says: Jack L. Davis earned his Cincinnati PhD in 1977 and taught at Illinois Chicago from 1977 to 1993.
Kosso’s CV records her 1993 Illinois Chicago ancient-history PhD and research assistance for Professor Jack Davis there in 1988–1989.
Jack E. Davis is the author of The Gulf and An Everglades Providence, affiliated with Alabama Birmingham.
John Anthony Davis is a historian of modern Italy, Oxford PhD, with Warwick and Connecticut appointments.
The John Davis candidate is John Henry Davis, history professor at Southwestern at Memphis and author of St. Mary’s Cathedral.
John R. Davis researches British and German history and heritage, with publications including The Victorians and Germany.
John P. Davis, author of Russia in the Time of Cholera, earned his PhD at Kentucky and teaches at Hopkinsville Community College.
J. C. Davis is James Colin Davis, professor of English history at East Anglia, previously at Massey.

notes: None of the six candidates is the UIC archaeologist. The supplied Illinois Urbana-Champaign 1956 doctorate conflicts with his Cincinnati 1977 PhD; supervisor identification rests on the student’s UIC connection.

who: Richard W. (Richard Whitlock) Davis, historian of Britain, UC Riverside 1964–1969, Columbia PhD reported as 1963.

The candidate authority expands Richard W. Davis to Richard Whitlock Davis and identifies Dissent in Politics and his Washington University appointment.

notes: The candidate’s work and Riverside career match the supervisor. The obituary gives 1963 for the doctorate, versus 1964 in the supplied record.
